title: Notice of Intent NECSAS
description: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Acquisition and Grants Office (AGO) Corporate Services Acquisition Division (CSAD), located in Silver Spring, MD, proposes to modify contract 1305M421DNAAA0016 on the basis of other than full and open competition in support of the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), Safety and Environmental Compliance Office (SECO), Environmental Compliance and Sustainability Division (ECSD). NOAA SECO requires additional ceiling capacity on IDIQ 1305M421DNAAA0016 for the remainder of the ordering period to procure technical professional services. These services are required to conduct comprehensive environmental, safety, and occupational health compliance audits at approximately 235 NOAA facilities in support of the NOAA Environmental Compliance and Safety Assessment System (NECSAS). SECO�s role in ensuring environmental compliance for NOAA Line and Staff Offices includes completing impact assessments, consultations, authorizations, and approvals required for proposed projects such as construction, renovation, as well as property acquisition and disposal. SECO is receiving a significant increase in the number of required projects for environmental compliance review. The NECSAS program requires a consistent, dedicated core audit team to maintain institutional knowledge across a diverse portfolio of Tier I, II, and III sites. The current Base IDIQ tasks include: Task 1: Environmental Compliance, Safety and Occupational Health Assessments Task 2: NEPA and Related Support Task 3: Floodplain and Wetlands Surveys Task 4: Hazardous Material Surveys Task 5: Environmental Site Assessments Task 6: Site Characterization, Remediation and Restoration Services Task 7: Data Management (e.g., Smartsheet/CPTrack) Task 8: Support Implementing the NOAA Environmental Management System Task 9: Building/Structural Demolition Related to Environmental Site Restoration Task 10: Support of Sustainability and Energy Program In accordance with 10 U.S.C. 3204(f) and 41 U.S.C. 3304(f), as implemented by Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) FAR 6.103, the NOAA intends to award a contract modification to AECOM Technical Services, Inc. Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract number 1305M421DNAAA0016. The contract will be modified to increase the ceiling value by $700,000.00, increasing the overall total contract ceiling value from $4,300,000.00 to $5,000,000.00. The ordering period end date remains unchanged as September 29, 2026. This ceiling increase is driven by increased demand for technical services rather than an adjustment to the contractual unit prices. The requested ceiling increase of $700,000 is derived from rigorous historical rate analysis of completed task orders for similar NECSAS compliance services, ensuring the ceiling adjustment is directly aligned with demonstrated program volume and actual mission requirements. The cumulative total value of task orders issued to date has reached 99.48% of the current ceiling, with less than 30-days remaining on the life of the contract. This notice is issued for informational purposes and not a request for competitive proposals. No solicitation is available. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. If no sufficient response is received, the ceiling will be increased without further notice. A determination to not compete the proposed action based on responses from this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Any interested party may submit a statement of capabilities in response to this notice of intent by no later than 15 days from the date of this announcement. Responses to this notice must be sent via email to Daphney.Jean-Minter@noaa.gov, Tania Gates@noaa.gov and Patrill.Smith-Moody@noaa.gov. No phone calls will be accepted.

title: MRTC Parking Lot Refresh
description: Marine Forces Special Operations Command, (MARSOC), Marine Raider Center (MRC), Camp Lejeune, NC has a requirement to repair/fill cracks and seal approximately 130,000 square feet of parking lot at RR450 parking lots. The general scope of work includes cleaning, filling, smoothing, and sealing both parking lots around RR450. The following Objectives are provided: 1. Mandatory Site Visit and Base Access Requirements A mandatory site visit will be conducted on 27 August at 0900 EST at the Building RR450 parking lot, Stone Bay, MCB Camp Lejeune, NC. Mandatory Attendance: Attendance at this site visit is mandatory. Only those vendors who attend the site visit in its entirety will be eligible to submit quotes in response to this solicitation. Quotes received from vendors who did not attend the site visit will be rejected without evaluation. Base Access Request Deadline: To gain access to the MARFORSOC compound at Stone Bay, contractor personnel must be vetted. Vendors must submit their base access request documentation to the Contracting Officer (Samuel Williams) and the Contract Specialist via email no later than 24 August. Access Request Content: The access request must be submitted on the visiting company's official stationery, signed by a company authority, and contain the following information for each attendee (limit of 2 attendees per company): Full Legal Name (Last, First, Middle) Date of Birth Place of Birth Citizenship Driver's License Number and State of Issuance 2. Proposal Submission Instructions Eligible offerors (who attended the mandatory site visit) shall submit their proposals via email to the Contracting Office. Proposals must be submitted in three (3) separate and distinct volumes as outlined below. Page limits must be strictly adhered to; any pages exceeding the limit will not be evaluated. Volume Title Page Limit Submission Requirements Volume I Technical Capability 6 Pages Max Technical Approach, Equipment List, Personnel Overview, and Draft Construction Phasing Plan. Volume II Past Performance 2 Pages Max Up to three (3) Past Performance References of similar scope and complexity. Volume III Price No Limit Completed SF 1449 Schedule of Supplies/Services, Price Breakdown, and Representations & Certifications. 3. Volume Content Requirements A. Volume I: Technical Capability The Technical Volume must clearly demonstrate the offeror's capability to perform the requirements set forth in the Statement of Work (SOW). Boilerplate or repeating the SOW language without detail is unacceptable. The volume must include: Technical Approach: A detailed narrative describing how the offeror will execute SOW Objectives #1 through #6, specifically outlining the crack cleaning process, crack-filling application (Objective #2), seal coat application and mixing ratio (Objective #3), restriping and stenciling (Objective #4), parking block replacement and installation (Objective #5), and the handicap sign post installations (Objective #6). Draft Construction Phasing Plan: A draft plan showing how the offeror will execute the work while maintaining at least fifty percent (50%) parking capacity operational continuity at Building RR450 at all times. The plan must include a tentative Gantt chart schedule within the 120-day Period of Performance and explain how emergency vehicle access will be guaranteed. Security and Base Access Compliance: A brief statement acknowledging and demonstrating a plan to comply with Camp Lejeune base access regulations (NCIC checks) and coordinating with MARSOC-provided escorts. B. Volume II: Past Performance Offerors shall submit up to three (3) past performance references for federal, state, local, or commercial contracts executed within the past three (3) years that are similar in scope and complexity to the RR450 requirement (e.g., parking lot sealing, crack filling, and striping requirements exceeding 50,000 sq ft). Each reference must include: Contract Number, Customer Name, and Point of Contact (Email and Phone). Period of Performance and Total Contract Dollar Value. A brief description of the work performed, highlighting similarities to the RR450 scope of work, specifically mentioning the total square footage treated and whether phasing or escort requirements were managed. Note: Offerors may submit standard reference letters in lieu of, or in addition to, the contact list. C. Volume III: Price The offeror shall submit a fully completed SF 1449 schedule with firm-fixed-prices (FFP) for the single, lump-sum CLIN (0001). The offeror must also submit a supporting price breakdown detailing direct material costs, direct labor costs (complying with Davis-Bacon Wage Determination No. NC20260090), mobilization, project management/overhead, and bond costs.

title: Ireland – Medical practice and related services – Cork County Council's Framework for Provision of Occupational Therapist Services
description: Cork County Council intends to form a multi-party framework of persons suitably qualified in the field of occupational therapy, to provide the required services and advice in relation to applications for Housing Adaptation Grants for Older People and People with a Disability Grant Schemes for private houses and adaptations to local authority owned homes. The occupational therapist will be required to carry out an assessment of the needs of the applicant and works required and submit a written report to the Council with regards to the appropriateness of the works / adaptations sought. Cork County Council proposes to engage in a competitive process for the establishment of a multi-party framework agreement for the provision of occupational therapist assessments and reports. The framework agreement will be established with 10 or more economic operators, subject to that number meeting the minimum criteria and rules and as set out in the Tender Response Document. For the purposes of establishing the framework, the County area is divided into 10 lots / areas covering the administrative are of Cork County Council. The framework will consist of 10 separate frameworks one for each lot / area. It is envisaged that the framework will be further subdivided into two identical frameworks, one covering Local Authority owned homes under the Disabled Persons Grant Schemes and the other covering privately owned homes under the Housing Adaptation Grants for Older People and People with a Disability Schemes. Each of these lots will result in a separate framework of successful tenderers. Applicants can indicate which lot / area they wish to apply to be included (map provided showing lots). The framework for each lot / area will operate using the rotation method where a call-off contract may be awarded by application of the terms already laid down in the framework agreement. The framework agreement will be for a maximum period of 4 years.

title: FY26 Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) Pump Upfit
description: FY26 Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) Stormwater Pump Station - DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) stormwater pump station (PS), located in the Medical District on the Charleston Peninsula, is critical infrastructure for the City of Charleston (City). The MUSC drainage basin forms a topographic low point without a natural outlet, and the PS is required to facilitate drainage. Proposed improvements include: increased pumping capacity including both pump and discharge piping capacity; improved hydraulic configuration in the wet well and inflow chamber; enclosure and conditioning of the control room; elevating all critical electrical and HVAC equipment above the design flood elevation; replacement and upgrade of electrical, instrumentation and controls, security, and lighting; construction of a new transformer pad and installation of increased capacity transformer; replacement of both wet well inflow pipes to correct pipe slope; structural supports of pipes and transformer pad; construction of a permanent bypass connection; replacement of the chain link gate; and minor grading and landscaping around the perimeter slab. The project also includes temporary pumps and piping to maintain station operations during construction. MAGNITUDE OF WORK is estimated at: $5,000,000 TO $10,000,000 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 237110, Water and Sewer Line Related THIS ACQUISITION IS UNRESTRICTED. title: FY26 Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) Pump Upfit
description: FY26 Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) Stormwater Pump Station - DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) stormwater pump station (PS), located in the Medical District on the Charleston Peninsula, is critical infrastructure for the City of Charleston (City). The MUSC drainage basin forms a topographic low point without a natural outlet, and the PS is required to facilitate drainage. Proposed improvements include: increased pumping capacity including both pump and discharge piping capacity; improved hydraulic configuration in the wet well and inflow chamber; enclosure and conditioning of the control room; elevating all critical electrical and HVAC equipment above the design flood elevation; replacement and upgrade of electrical, instrumentation and controls, security, and lighting; construction of a new transformer pad and installation of increased capacity transformer; replacement of both wet well inflow pipes to correct pipe slope; structural supports of pipes and transformer pad; construction of a permanent bypass connection; replacement of the chain link gate; and minor grading and landscaping around the perimeter slab. The project also includes temporary pumps and piping to maintain station operations during construction. MAGNITUDE OF WORK is estimated at: $5,000,000 TO $10,000,000 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 237110, Water and Sewer Line Related THIS ACQUISITION IS UNRESTRICTED. title: 2WS/557WW Demountable Walls
description: PRE-SOLICITATION OFFUTT AFB 2WS/557WW Demountable Walls 55 CONS/PKB - FA4600 106 PEACEKEEPER LN, STE 2N3, OFFUTT AFB, NE 68113 27 August 2026 Product/Service Code: N017 NAICS code: 238390 Place of Performance: Offutt AFB, Nebraska Proposed Set Aside: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside DESCRIPTION 55CONS intends to award a sole source, firm-fixed-price contract to Encompass Corporation for the reconfiguration of Haworth Demountable Walls for the 2WS and the 557WW. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes; however, interested parties who believe they can meet the requirements listed below may submit capability statements for consideration. Please see the attached PWS's for further specifications of this requirement. Summary of Performance Work Statements: 2WS 4.1 Wall Modifications Rooms 1340 & 1342 Partition: Disassemble existing demountable wall panels dividing Rooms 1340 and 1342. Salvage, inspect, and reuse hardware to relocate and install the wall, completely enclosing Room 1342 as an independent space. Room 1332 Reconfiguration: Install new demountable partition walls to divide the current footprint into two (2) fully enclosed offices and a shared communal area, including all ceiling tracks, floor channels, acoustic seals, and trim. Room 1343 Deconstruction: Fully disassemble and remove demountable walls, door frames, and hardware from Room 1343 to restore it to an open-plan layout. Hand over salvaged components to the 557th WW Facility Manager (or legally dispose/recycle as directed). Rooms 1220, 1221, & 1222 Merger: Disassemble and remove the demountable partitions dividing Rooms 1220, 1221, and 1222 to merge them into a single, open-concept footprint. Patch and repair affected ceiling grids, floor surfaces, and adjacent walls. 4.2 Door Installations The Contractor shall install four (4) 40-inch demountable door panels configured to open inward at the following locations: Room 1342: One (1) door panel. Room 1332: Two (2) door panels (one for each of the newly constructed offices). Room 1332 (from Room 1320): One (1) door panel. 4.3 HVAC (Government Furnished Property/Work) Air Transfer Grilles: Install return air transfer grilles between Room 1340 and the new office space, and between the new offices within Room 1332 to balance static pressure and ensure proper airflow distribution. Note: This specific task (4.3) will be accomplished by the 557th Weather Wing Facilities office and is excluded from the contractor's performance requirements. B185 The contractor shall perform the following teardown, relocation, and installation tasks: Room L422 Relocation and Reconfiguration: Dismantle and move the L423 four (4) West wall panels to the East by approximately 8ft. Utilize the existing L422 door and glass panel to establish the new L422 door space. Room L423 Expansion and Reconfiguration: Reclaim and integrate existing L423 and legacy L422 demountable panels to expand the designated work area. Use on hand demountable wall stock to fill in existing wall gaps to complete the room (~25ft). Install double solid wood doors in the Southeast corner of the room, complete with appropriate framing and HAWORTH-compatible commercial hardware. Final door location determined at install (adjust as needed to accommodate install) Room L421 Configuration Use existing material stock to install new walls to close in Collaboration and training space. Approximately 25 linear feet of panels, configured as two intersecting runs of approximately 23 feet and 2 feet. Final adjustment allowed during install. Extract the legacy L423 door and associate hardware and re-install door to serve as the new entrance for Room L421. TBD during install (Adjustments allowed as needed) This requirement will be awarded using RFO part 12 Simplified Procedures. The award will be made prior to 30 September 2026. If you have any questions please reach out via email to A1C Hunter Hendrix (hunter.hendrix.1@us.af.mil) or TSgt Jennifer Prestridge (jennifer.prestridge.1@us.af.mil).

title: Germany – Application work of anti-corrosive coatings – Instandsetzung D002 Stahlviadukt Barmbek , Projekt Brücken Barmbek
description: Bei dem Brückenbauwerk aus dem Jahre 1918 handelt es sich um eine Fachwerkbrücke mit 18 Überbauten in Trog- und Deckkonstruktion mit Tonnenblechen. Die Spannweiten der einzelnen Überbauten liegen zwischen 18,6 m und 48,5 m. Das Bauwerk überbrückt mehrere Gleise der HOCHBAHN, Teile eines Betriebshofes der HOCHBAHN, S-Bahngleise, eine S-Bahn-Abstellanlage, ein Güterumgehungsgleis mit Oberleitung, private und öffentliche Flächen sowie die Straßenkreuzung Hellbrookstraße/Rübenkamp auf eine Höhe von bis zu 14 m über GOK. Im Wesentlichen sollen folgende Maßnahmen durchgeführt werden: - Lokale Instandsetzung des Korrosionsschutzes durch Ausbesserung. - Stahlbauarbeiten, Stahlbauinstandsetzung - Betoninstandsetzung - Teilerneuerung der Entwässerungsleitungen Bei dem Auftrag handelt es sich um umfangreiche und anspruchsvolle Korrosionsschutz-, Stahlbau- und Betonerhaltungsmaßnahmen mit hoher Anforderung an den Arbeitsschutz und die Durchführungsqualität.

title: Notice of Intent to Award Sole Source - SimX VR Medical Simulation
description: The 97th MDG requires two virtual reality headsets with licensing software to conduct realistic medical training with a wide variety of types of practice from combat lifesaver and first responder. The 97th MDG intends to make a sole source award to SimX Inc (CAGE: 79S56), due to being the only source capable of providing the proprietary software-based platform for conducting realistic medical training which is compatible with their headset. It is designed for effectiveness in a wide variety of settings and for a wide variety of types of practice, from combat lifesaver and first responder to high acuity in-hospital care. The SimX technology was developed in part with funds from the Federal Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) program. The SBIR program is used by the Federal Government to enable the development of technologies with dual use potential within the Government as well as the commercial sector. The SBIR program is competitively selected, and a cost reasonableness assessment is made by US Government contracting officers during selection. Under the Federal SBA SBIR/STTR Policy Directive, this assessment may be relied upon by contracting officers to satisfy the need for competition and serves as a Federal Justification for Other than Full and Open Competition (JOFOC / also known as a "sole source justification"). Additionally, because SimX owns the SBIR Data Rights and patent(s) in the technology, no other company may produce and/or sell the same technology without a license or distribution agreement from SimX. The proposed contract action for the Government intends to solicit from a single source under the authority of RFO 6.103-1 and 10 U.S.C 3204(a)(1). This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive proposals, and no solicitation document exists for the requirement. Sources interested in responding to this notice are required to submit a capability statement that includes technical data and cost information, sufficient detail and with convincing evidence that clearly demonstrates the capability to meet the requirement. title: Boiler Inspection and Repairs
description: The Contractor shall perform a comprehensive inspection of all 13 gas boilers and calibrate the associated gas sensors. title: ITP Training Dormitory Design Build Construction, Comayagua, Honduras
description: This is a sources sought notice for information only. This sources sought is for the purpose of conducting market research to provide data for planning purposes. This sources sought synopsis announcement does not constitute a formal solicitation, and is not a request for proposal, request for quote, invitation for bid, does not obligate the government to award a contract, issue a solicitation, reimburse respondents for any proposal preparation and/or submittal costs, nor does its issuance in any way restrict the Government as to its ultimate acquisition approach. The Government will not pay for any materials provided in response to this notice and submittals will not be returned to the sender. The Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL), U.S. Embassy Tegucigalpa, intends to construct a new student dormitory facility within the Instituto T�cnico Policial (ITP) Training Compound located in Comayagua, Honduras. The objective of this project is to provide a complete Design-Review, Engineering, Construction Documents, Construction, Testing, Commissioning, and Turnover solution for the construction of a new dormitory facility at the Instituto T�cnico Policial (ITP) in Comayagua, Honduras The proposed facility is intended to accommodate approximately 156 male police students and includes dormitory sleeping areas, restroom facilities, shower facilities, and laundry areas required for daily operation of the training center. The project has been intentionally developed utilizing a simplified and highly repetitive construction approach intended to facilitate construction, reduce project duration, simplify maintenance requirements, and maximize long-term operational value. The Government has developed a Conceptual Design Package, further referred to as Bridging Documents (See Appendix A), establishing the intended facility configuration, capacities, architectural appearance, minimum material requirements, and minimum technical standards. These documents are included as Government Reference Drawings and Technical Appendices and form part of this Statement of Work. The Contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, engineering services, professional certifications, materials, equipment, transportation, tools, permits, testing, quality control, safety measures, and incidentals necessary to design and construct a complete and operational facility. The completed facility shall be safe, durable, maintainable, code-compliant, and fully operational upon final Government acceptance. This is not a solicitation nor will a solicitation package be issued as a result of this announcement, and no award shall be made as a result of this announcement. description: This is not a solicitation for a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a commitment, implied or otherwise, that Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR), will take procurement action in this matter. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this posting. The purpose of this notification is to inform industry of the Government's intent and to gain knowledge of other potentially qualified sources. The CBP Office of Professional Responsibility (OPR) intends to issue a sole-source, Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to OPSEC SECURITY INC, located at 1857 COLONIAL VILLAGE LN, LANCASTER, PA 17601-6702; UEI Y1KQH3MMQPW5. This action falls under the authority of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) FAR 6.103-1[1] , "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." The applicable NAICS code is 326130, Laminated Plastics Plate, Sheet (Except Packaging), And Shape Manufacturing, with a Product Service Code (PSC) of 9330, Plastics Fabricated Materials. Brief Description of the Acquisition Requirement: The Government requires high-security holographic overlay laminate for credentials. Every credential issued consists of two (2) pouches: Pouch A and Pouch B. Pouch A is constructed of a see-through holographic security laminate specially designed to CBP/DHS credential dimensions and contains DHS- specific holograms embedded with a DHS seal inlay. Pouch B is constructed of see-through holographic security laminate specially designed to CBP/DHS credential dimensions and contains DHS official seals and acronyms. The required pouches are highly unique, proprietary, high-security, holographic overlay laminate pouch sets. OPSEC SECURITY, INC. holds the design plates and is the sole manufacturer of this one-of-a-kind type of DHS/CBP laminate. OPSEC SECURITY, INC. is the sole manufacturer, seller, and distributor of this DHS-specific high security laminate. No authorized resellers exist, and no other products meet operational needs, security, or compatibility requirements. All DHS credentials must be 100% consistent in size, design, embedded security features, and technical specifications in order to maintain positive identity identification and authority authentication of the DHS credential bearer. There can be no differentiation in the visual appearance or feel of these credentials. Plastic without the DHS high-security features is not an acceptable substitute and will not be considered. Submission Information: There are no solicitation documents available. However, a responsible source that believes it can meet the Government's requirement for this specific high-security holographic laminate may submit a complete technical package providing clear and convincing evidence of their capabilities. The response must demonstrate the ability to provide high security holographic laminate that is 100% compatible with CBP�s current high security holographic laminate for credentials and must be accompanied by a statement confirming the offeror's willingness to provide a full performance guarantee for the fit, form, and function of the items without access to OPSEC�s proprietary data. CBP credentials are 100% consistent with DHS and all component agency credentials. All information furnished shall be in writing and must contain sufficient detail to allow the Government to make a determination of the offeror's capabilities. CBP has appointed an Ombudsman to consider and facilitate the resolution of concerns from offerors. Concerned parties should address their concerns to the Contracting Officer prior to consulting the Ombudsman. The CBP Ombudsman contact information is: Judith A. Simpson@cbp.dhs.gov. Responses must be received no later than September 11, 2026. Responses should be submitted via email to: Contracting Officer Erin Schwam, Email: ERIN.SCHWAM@cbp.dhs.gov. No phone calls will be accepted. Late responses will not be considered. title: Production, Translation, and Broadcast Services for Weekly Radio Program - "Sous L'Arbre � Palabre"
description: STATEMENT OF WORK (Incorporated in full from the Government-furnished SOW; reproduced here for completeness of the solicitation package.) Background The U.S. Embassy in Guinea's radio program, "Sous L'Arbre � Palabre," is currently broadcast in six languages across Guinea. The radio show highlights U.S. embassy engagement in Guinea, U.S. companies and other U.S. organizations operating in Guinea, U.S. government exchange alumni, and other Guineans that share U.S. values and priorities. The podcast-style program explores inspiring stories and transformative initiatives across various themes, including healthcare, security, education, business, and entrepreneurship. The target audience includes a wide range of listeners, especially those with limited internet access, literacy, or French language skills. By showcasing these stories, the Embassy aims to connect with all Guineans on issues of importance to the U.S. Embassy in Guinea. Objectives The primary objective of this project is to produce, translate, and broadcast a 20-minute, weekly radio show, "Sous L'Arbre � Palabre," on behalf of the U.S. Embassy in Guinea. The program aims to: Highlight U.S. Engagement in Guinea: Provide a platform for dialogue between the embassy, local partners, and the Guinean public to highlight key areas of U.S. engagement in Guinea, including but not limited to: U.S. businesses and commercial investment in Guinea, key health and security initiatives, and educational and exchange opportunities offered by the U.S. government. Promote U.S.-Guinea Shared Values: Through inspirational stories and interviews, encourage attitudes and behaviors that align with the values and goals of the U.S. embassy and its partners. Reach a National Audience: Engage with audiences across Guinea, particularly those with limited internet access, literacy, or French language skills. Broadcast languages: French, Poular, Sousou, Malink�, Kissi, and Guerz�. Broadcast in all four regions: Forest region: Kissidougou, N'Z�r�kore, Gu�ck�dou; Upper Guinea: Kankan, Siguiri, Faranah; Middle Guinea: Labe, Mamou; and Coastal Guinea: Kindia, Boke Period of Performance The period of performance for this project is October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2027. During this period, the contractor will record new twenty-minute radio programs; translate newly recorded and previously recorded Embassy-provided programs, as specified in the Service Delivery and Pricing Schedule; and broadcast completed programs weekly across all regions in Guinea. Key Milestones: Weekly Radio Shows: First Show Broadcast: October 11, 2026 Subsequent Weekly Broadcasts: Every Sunday at 15:30, unless the parties mutually agree in writing to a different recurring broadcast day and/or time. Final Show Broadcast: September 5, 2027 Monthly Reports: First Monday of each month, beginning November 2, 2026. Final Evaluation Meeting: Week of September 27, 2027 Disclaimer: Dates are tentative and may be adjusted to reflect solicitation, evaluation, and award timelines, and in response to force majeure/acts of God. Prior-Contract Episode Inventory The Embassy will provide the Contractor with: 13 French-language episodes produced under a prior contract requiring translation and broadcasting under this contract. 9 episodes produced and translated under a prior contract requiring broadcasting only under this contract. At the beginning of the period of performance for the contract envisaged by the current solicitation , some of the these previous contract episodes may still be in production or translation and may therefore not be immediately available to the contractor. The Service Delivery and Pricing Schedule at section IV above reflects only the services to be performed under this contract. Each service is considered a separate unit of performance, and an episode may require any of the following combinations of service elements: Recording, translation, and broadcast; Translation and broadcast only; Broadcast only. Accordingly, services completed under the prior contract are not included as service units under this contract; only the remaining translation and/or broadcasting services to be performed by the contractor are reflected in the applicable service quantities. title: 6515--VISN 8 Situate Detection System
description: Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice Page 5 of 5 Sources Sought Notice *= Required Field Sources Sought Notice Page 1 of 5 THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation for bids, proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement. The responses received from interested contractors will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), NCO 08- is conducting a market research survey to identify potential qualified sources capable of providing Sponge Detection System for The Department of Veterans Affairs, NCO 8, throughout twelve VISN 8 medical centers, at a firm fixed price. BACKGROUND: VISN 8 currently does not utilize a lap sponge detection system other than manual sponge counts conducted by surgical staff. The absence of an automated detection solution increases the risk of human error and retained surgical items, which can compromise patient safety and lead to adverse events. SCOPE OF REQUIREMENT The Government requires an integrated retained surgical item (RSI) detection system that serves as an adjunct to established manual sponge counting procedures. The purpose of the system is to provide an independent method of detecting retained radiofrequency (RF)-tagged laparotomy sponges during operative procedures in order to enhance patient safety and reduce the potential for retained surgical items. The following items are manufactured by Medtronic (or equal, if applicable): Situate Console X Body Scanner Lite Room Scanner X Complete Care Service Plan for Situate System X Console Key Salient Characteristics: All components Made in the U.S.A. Automated non-handheld RF scanning beneath the patient capable of detecting RF-tagged surgical sponges during operative procedures A handheld environmental scanner capable of locating RF-tagged sponges within the operating room, including linens, waste containers, prep areas, and surrounding equipment Workflow guidance that provides standardized prompts supporting consistent use of the system across multiple VISN 8 medical centers Verification of completed scans prior to surgical closure Documentation supporting incorporation of scan results into the patient's medical record Manufacturer-supported software updates, preventive maintenance, technical support, replacement parts and complete care service plan throughout the contract period Services Required: Timely delivery of the Medtronic Situate Laparoscopic Detection System Deliver comprehensive user training to all locations Provide hands-on training sessions Train biomedical engineering and technical support staff Provide on site clinical support Deliver ongoing clinical and technical support Conduct preventive maintenance as per manufacturer standards Supply required parts, consumables, and maintenance materials Provide a comprehensive warranty covering system components, accessories, software, and workmanship for the agreed upon warranty period RESPONSES MUST INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING INFORMATION: Company Name, Address, Size Standard, UEI#, Cage Code Description of your company's experience providing and installing institutional-grade mental health or behavioral health furniture of similar scope and complexity. Identify whether you are a manufacturer, authorized dealer/distributor, or reseller of the specified products (Medtronic or equivalent). If you intend to team or subcontract, identify your teaming partners and their roles. Contract number (If on existing government contract that can be ordered off of) Point of Contact name, phone number, and email address *NOTE Acquisitions will only be set aside for SDVOSBs/VOSBs if two or more responses that meet the Non-manufacturer Rule are received with the required information listed above, by the due date specified below. Responses are due to Todd Pappas at todd.pappas@va.gov by 12:00 PM EST on September 11, 2026. No submissions will be accepted after this date and time. This is a RFI Notice and submissions will be used for informational and planning purposes only. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. Disclaimer and Important Notes: This RFI does not obligate the Government to award a contract or otherwise pay for the information provided in response. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. The Government will treat any information received as proprietary and will not share such information with other companies. Any organization responding to this RFI should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. title: Non-Research Long-Term Care facility needed for the enrichment and socialization of Non-Human Primate colony
description: Amendment 3 is being issued to post a revised copy of the solicitation and extend the due date to 12:00 PM EDT on September 11, 2026. Amendment 2 is being issued to post the Q&A and a modified solicitation package. It also extends the due date to July 23, 2026. Amendment 1 is being issued to extend the due date to 07/20/2026. Another amendment will be issued once Q&A and the revised solicitation is ready. The purpose of this acquisition is to secure permanent housing of approximately 130 NHPs and the responsibility for providing them with a safe, compliant, and humane long-term sanctuary with a limited lead time. The contractor shall implement structured social group formation, behavioral rehabilitation, provide comprehensive lifetime care, and have sole custody and ownership for each animal. The overall objective is to ensure the seamless and humane transfer of all CDC animals into naturalistic and enriched environments that support their physical and behavioral health, within facilities that are compliant with standards set by the GFAS and that maintain these animals as set by applicable animal welfare regulations and standards. The facility must be GFAS-accredited and a sanctuary at which no research or breeding will take place. The facility must not buy, sell, or trade animals or sell animal byproducts. Direct public contact should be prohibited. The facility shall also provide species-appropriate habitat and enclosure design that supports the expression of natural behaviors.

title: Sources Sought Notice - AT Courtyard, Bettis Laboratory - Department of Energy
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION Notice Type: Sources Sought Notice (W911WN26R1CIY) Subject: Bettis Laboratory "AT Courtyard" Construction Project Primary NAICS Code: 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction (Size Standard: $45.0 Million) Alternative NAICS Considered: 238910 � Site Preparation Contractors (Size Standard: $19.0 Million) Place of Performance: DOE Bettis Laboratory, West Mifflin, Pennsylvania 15122 Response Deadline: 12:00 P.M. E.T., 11 September 2026 2.0 INTRODUCTION & OBJECTIVE This is a Sources Sought Notice only. This is not a solicitation announcement, requesting proposals or bids. Its purpose is to conduct market research to determine the interest, capability, and availability of qualified businesses�specifically including small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses (SDVOSB), women-owned small businesses (WOSB), and 8(a) certified small businesses�to perform a non-commercial civil utility, hardscaping, and landscaping construction project at the Department of Energy (DOE) Bettis Laboratory in West Mifflin, PA. The project is being managed on behalf of the Government by Fluor Marine Propulsion, LLC (FMP), the operating contractor for the Bettis Laboratory under the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program / Naval Nuclear Laboratory (NNL). Anticipated Construction Cost is between $2,500,000.00 and $5,500,000.00. 3.0 PROJECT DESCRIPTION & SCOPE OF WORK The "AT Courtyard" project involves comprehensive civil site preparation, utility line demolition and relocation, utility main installations, hardscaping, structural concrete and masonry, structural pergola erection, and advanced landscaping at a secure facility. The selected contractor must be capable of executing work across the following core technical specification areas: 3.1 Site Preparation, Earthwork & Demolition Selective Demolition: Demolition and safe removal of selected existing site elements, including cutting and sealing underground utilities. Coordination of work to prevent disruption of ongoing, adjacent FMP facility operations. Site Clearing: Clearing of vegetation, grubbing, topsoil stripping, and stockpiling/stabilizing soil. Earth Moving & Dewatering: Significant excavation, grading, proof-rolling subgrades using 10-ton compaction rollers, backfilling, and structural fill placement. Control of groundwater and surface runoff during construction to keep excavations dry and subgrades stable. 3.2 Underground Civil Utilities Sanitary Sewers: Installation of green SDR-35 PVC gravity sanitary sewer piping (15-inch and smaller), precast concrete manholes with butyl rubber joint sealants, and coal tar epoxy waterproofing. High-requirement testing including vacuum testing of manholes (ASTM C1244), low-pressure air testing, and deflection testing using GO-NO-GO mandrels. Utility Line Removal & Abandonment: Disconnection, capping, and plugging of existing utilities in place or complete removal. Permanent valve abandonment matching existing site pavement or landscape conditions. Site City Water Utility Distribution Piping: Installation of AWWA C906/ASTM F714 high-density polyethylene (HDPE) water mains. Requires certified heat-fusion jointing (butt/socket fusion) with comprehensive data logging. Cleaning, pressure testing, and disinfection (AWWA C651) with mandatory water-quality lab verification. Storm Utility Drainage Piping: Installation of smooth-wall corrugated HDPE storm sewer and combination underdrain piping, precast concrete inlets (ASTM C913), and reinforced cast-in-place concrete trench drains with secured stainless-steel grates. Site Natural-Gas Distribution: Installation of ASTM D2513 medium-density PE gas piping (SDR 11) using electro-fusion joints (ASTM F1055). Installation of underground PE ball valves, cast-iron valve boxes, and nitrogen-gas pneumatic pressure/leak testing witnessed by FMP. 3.3 Concrete, Masonry & Paving Cast-In-Place Concrete: Providing, forming, reinforcing, placing, and curing of concrete wall footings, pipe bollard footings, thrust blocks, and encasements. Compressive strengths of up to 5,000 psi. Extensive quality assurance including on-site aggregate sampling, slump tests, and laboratory cylinder compression testing. Unit Masonry: Construction of brick and concrete masonry unit (CMU) structures including retaining walls, raised seating areas, and custom precast concrete caps. Paving & Decomposed Granite: Installation of exterior concrete roadway and walkway pavements over aggregate subbases, specialized joint sealants (multi-component jet-fuel-resistant elastomeric/urethane formulations), and stabilized decomposed granite utilizing organic binding agents around tree plantings. 3.4 Site Furnishings, Hardscaping & Landscaping Site Furnishings & Pergolas: Installation of high-end, freestanding site furnishings including custom steel benches, picnic tables, cast aluminum chairs, steel planters, double-pedestal low-profile fiberglass graphic panel signs, and a large-scale structural aluminum pergola (nominal dimensions 10' H x 16' W x 16' D) secured to structural concrete footings. All metal elements must meet Buy America Standards. Soil Preparation & Plants: Extensive landscaping including performance-tested planting soils, multi-layered engineered soil profiles for deep containers/rooftop-style planters (rooflite system), weed-control geotextiles, and organic/mineral mulching. Planting and 12-month warranty establishment of specified trees, shrubs, ornamental grasses, and ground covers. 4.0 SPECIAL CONTRACTOR REQUIREMENTS & SITE CONDITIONS Secure Facility Operations: The project is located within a highly secure government nuclear laboratory. The selected contractor must strictly comply with the following facility access control measures: Prohibited Items: Personal electronic devices, including but not limited to cellular phones, smart watches, tablets, cameras, and recording devices, are strictly prohibited within the secure perimeter. Citizenship Requirements: All contractor and subcontractor personnel requiring site access must be citizens of the United States. Dual citizenship is not permitted; all personnel must be U.S. citizens only. Identification & Entry Vetting: All personnel�including prime contractors, subcontractors, and even temporary delivery drivers�must possess a state-issued Real ID and successfully complete and pass a background check administered by the Department of Energy (DOE) prior to receiving security badges or being granted physical access to the facility. Logistics & Disposal: Contractors must comply with strict physical security protocols, vehicle searches, and FMP-specific hauling and waste disposal regulations. Personnel Certifications: PE Pipe Fusion: Technicians executing heat-fusion on gas or water piping must hold current certifications in accordance with ASTM F3190 / ASTM F2620. Landscape Supervisor: Field operations must be supervised full-time by an individual with a minimum of five (5) years of experience in landscape installation, holding a certification from the National Association of Landscape Professionals (e.g., Landscape Industry Certified Technician - Exterior). Testing & Inspection: Extensive field-testing is required throughout execution, to be performed by an independent, qualified laboratory (e.g., concrete strength, compaction, sewer hydrostatic/air pressure, gas pneumatic, soil chemistry/fertility). 5.0 SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS Interested firms who believe they possess the capability to perform this work are requested to submit a response containing the following information: Company Profile: Company Name and address. Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email). Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code. Business Size and Socio-Economic Status under NAICS 237990 and/or 238910 (e.g., Small Business, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, HUBZone). In your best business judgement, indicate which NAICS Code is most appropriate for this projec

title: Perforated Window Film
description: This contract is in support of the United States Marine Corps Recruiting Command (MCRC) Branding Program for each of the six (6) Marine Corps Districts (MCD), which are located throughout the United States, overseas and its territories. The use of branded locations, emphasizing the approved Marine Corps colors, symbols, themes, furnishings, and lighting effects will help distinguish Marine Corps recruiting offices from recruiting offices of other Armed Services, providing a distinct recruiting advantage vis-a-vis other Services. The appearance of the branded offices leaves a positive impression not just with prospects, but their parents and other influencers as well. MCRC is taking steps to improve physical security of recruiting facilities. MCRC intends to utilize perforated window film on the glass surfaces of storefront recruiting facilities in order to provide concealment, more specifically, protection from observation. It is necessary to have a means of obscuring the view of Marine recruiting station from the outside as a force protection measure. It is also necessary that, where practical, the Marines maintain visibility of the area outside of their office in order to maintain their situational awareness. This will provide them with the possibility of early warning, if a potential aggressor is approaching the office or preparing to commit some type of hostile or unlawful act, outside the office. Perforated window film will allow for MCRC Branding Program success, while providing increased security for recruiting personnel and individuals visiting recruiting offices. As a part of this requirement, the current storefront glass graphics will be removed, and new perforated window film will be installed to span the entire glass window/door surface. Perforated window film will be installed on existing facilities that have no storefront graphics. Additionally, perforated film will be replaced on existing facilities as required.

title: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR)/Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Program
description: The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) is soliciting proposals from small business concerns (SBCs) that possess the research and development (R&D) expertise to conduct innovative research that will contribute toward ARPA-H mission needs, Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR), and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) program objectives. Please see the cover page of the attachment "SBIR_STTR_BAA_FY26" for applicable Stage 1 and Stage 2 deadlines for each open topic. Please see the Attachment H "ARPA-H_SBP_Government_Answered_Questions" for responses to the Q&A period. The purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs are to: (a) stimulate technological innovation; (b) strengthen the role of small business in meeting Federal research/research & development (R/R&D) needs; (c) foster and encourage participation by socially and economically disadvantaged small business concerns and women-owned business concerns; and (d) increase private sector commercialization of innovations derived from Federal R/R&D, thereby increasing competition, productivity and economic growth. For purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs, a small business concern is any business concern that, on the date of award, (1) is organized for profit, with a place of business located in the United States, which operates primarily within the United States or which makes a significant contribution to the United States economy through payment of taxes or use of American products, materials or labor; (2) is in the legal form of an individual proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, corporation, joint venture, association, trust or cooperative, except that where the form is a joint venture, there must be less than 50 percent participation by foreign business entities in the joint venture; (3) more than 50% directly owned and controlled by one or more individuals (who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), other business concerns (each of which is more than 50% directly owned and controlled by individuals who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), or any combination of these; OR more than 50% owned by multiple venture capital operating companies, hedge funds, private equity firms, or any combination of these. No single venture capital operating company, hedge fund, or private equity firm may own more than 50% of the concern; AND, (4) has, including its affiliates, no more than 500 employees. Note: This size standard is established by law for the SBIR program, regardless of the NAICS Code assigned. See 13 C.F.R. � 121.702. AMENDMENT 01 - July 8, 2026: Amendment 01 of this solicitation extends the deadline for Stage 1 Solution Summaries from July 10, 2026 to July 17, 2026. Please check your email inbox for your Stage 1 encourage/discourage letters on or around August 17, 2026. Topic 05 Stage 1 letters and Stage 2 submission deadline will be distributed at a later date. THE FOLLOWING ARE THE CURRENTLY OPEN RESEARCH TOPICS. PLEASE SEE SECTION 8 OF THE BAA FOR FURTHER INFORMATION ARPA-H 01 -?Development of an annual test to inform women about their future fertility?-?The purpose of this topic is to discover new biomarkers that provide women with actionable data for fertility planning.? Results from this work will help inform the program manager regarding the feasibility of future programs focused on enhancing natural fertility before the need of IVF and guiding the development of women�s health monitoring and improvement tools. This work will develop a diagnostic test that can assess fertility status and generate an estimated timeline for the onset of infertility. This topic seeks to develop a test that is affordable, suitable for at least annual use, and provides user-friendly results for patients and care teams to support childbearing decisions.??? ARPA-H 02 -?Versatile Bioadhesives?- The purpose of this topic is to develop next-generation bioadhesive platforms that can safely and reliably seal, bond, and repair a wide range of tissues in challenging clinical conditions, including wet, bloody, and mechanically dynamic environments. These platforms may also be designed to deliver biologics or small molecules as part of treatment. The goal is to create bioadhesives with key performance attributes such as strong tissue adhesion, controlled degradation, reversibility, biocompatibility, and broad compatibility across multiple tissues and organs. If successful, this topic could enable widely deployable solutions for hemostasis, leak prevention, tissue repair, and device fixation, ultimately helping reduce complications and improve patient outcomes across many care settings ARPA-H 03 -?Universal Platform for Living Adaptive Toxin-removal (UNI-PLAT)?-?The purpose of this topic area is to catalyze the development of a universal, �plug-and-play� synthetic biology platform that enables next-generation microbial chassis capable of performing a broad array of programmable functions. While this solicitation primarily uses toxin removal as a proof-of-concept in relation to chronic disease management, the platform is intended to be adaptable to a range of challenges across industries such as environmental remediation, biomanufacturing, agriculture, holistic medicine, and therapeutic discovery. The broader goal is to create a stable, reliable, and easily reprogrammable microbial platform that demonstrates potential for cross-sector impact beyond the initial use case.? ARPA-H 04 -?Breaking Ground: The First Curative, Durable, Non-Surgical Therapy for Endometriosis?�?The purpose of this topic aims to develop treatments for endometriosis that are non-surgical. Proposers are expected to develop novel, non-surgical therapies to decrease the size or deactivate endometrial implants, to decrease inflammation cause by implants, and / or prevent growth or regrowth of the lesions. Broadly, this should be a novel, non-surgical, curative treatment for endometriosis. ARPA-H 05 -?ARPA-H Lineage Topic?-?The purpose of this topic supports the advancement, commercialization, and translation of technologies that originated from ARPA-H funded efforts. description: Amendment 1: The purpose of this amendment is to extend the quote due date to 11 Sep 26 at 9:00AM PST. Combined Synopsis/Solicitation & Notice of Intent General Information Details Notice ID: FA9302-27-Q-0001 Notice Type: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Contracting Office: AFTC/PZZG NAICS Code: 611699 - All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction PSC Code: U099 - Education/Training - Other or Other Education and Training Services Response Date: 11 September 2026, 09:00AM PST Description of Requirement This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 12.2, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The Department of War (DoW) intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Perris Valley Aviation Services Inc, for the procurement of services for Test Parachutist Program at Edwards AFB. Notice of Intent to Sole Source Subject Description Statutory Authority 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1 Justification There is reasonable basis to conclude that the agency can only be satisfied by Perris Valley Aviation Services, Inc. Since they are the only vendor that possesses the capability to support the drop zones, pads, and the vertical wind tunnel within 150 miles of Edwards AFB. The vendor must provide an owner-operated drop zone and aircraft. On-site maintenance facilities, FAA certified parachute riggers, and mechanics must be available. On-site vertical wind tunnel and on-site training facilities with air conditioning, padded flooring for packing of parachutes, and computers and televisions for training/debriefing purposes. Vendor must have both, door and ramp capable aircraft available for both day and night parachute operations. Skydive Perris is the only parachute operating location that currently has a wind tunnel on location. Skydive Perris is the only vendor that is currently capable of meeting the requirements of the Test Parachutist Program. Scope of Work The contractor shall provide aircraft, pilot, United States Parachute Association (USPA) course instructor(s), and facilities necessary to support the 412th OSS Test Parachutist Program (TPP) operations as defined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS) attached. Market Research A similar requirement was procured the prior year and a sources sought notice was posted in SAM.gov to find how many capable vendors would be capable of fulfilling that requirements based on the PWS. Only one response was received from BHPE LLC, stating that they were interested in this opportunity. An email was sent to them requesting their capabilities statement, but they were unresponsive. Additionally, the company is located in Oklahoma. That requirement and this current requirement calls out for the drop zones and helipad locations to be within 150 miles of Edwards AFB. If BHPE was given the opportunity to quote on this requirement, it is highly likely that they would subcontract to Perris Valley Aviation since no other small businesses are available in the local area. Other known possible sources of the service were also contacted to validate the past research. Small Business office found a potential vendor (Square One) that may be able to fulfill the service. Both Square One Parachutes and Skydive Elsinore, Inc were each contacted to which they responded that they could not provide the service required since they do not have the infrastructure in place for a vertical wind tunnel. FPDS were searched under keyword "Skydive" and limited to "Ca". All the yielded results were contract awards to Skydive Elsinore, Inc. Multiple agencies utilized their service, but they could not fulfill this requirement. Instructions to Interested Parties This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Applicable Provisions & Clauses The following FAR/RFO provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition: Provision/Clause Title FAR 52.212-1 Instructions to Offerors - Commercial Products and Commercial Services FAR 52.212-3 Offeror Representations and Certifications - Commercial Products and Commercial Services FAR 52.212-4 Contract Terms and Conditions - Commercial Products and Commercial Services

description: This notice is issued in accordance with the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, specifically RFO 12.102(a) (Restricting Competition) and RFO 5.101. The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price commercial construction contract on a sole source basis to PP91 Enterprises, Inc, (UEI: TK2SC8CCNUL4), an 8(a) small business. The Government has a requirement for the specialized mechanical and software re-configuration of the facility's existing HVAC System . The scope of work includes, but is not limited to: Re-programming and re-configuration of the chiller control sequences to align with updated building occupancy schedules. Integration of the mechanical piping and variable frequency drives (VFDs) between the chiller system and the ERU dampers. Testing, balancing, and commissioning of the combined HVAC/ERU loop to ensure optimal energy efficiency and air exchange metrics. Verification of compliance with building automation system (BAS) communication protocols. The Government intends to solicit and negotiate a sole-source contract with the Original Construction Contractor, for the following critical technical and warranty reasons: Warranty Integrity: The HVAC Chiller, air handlers, and ERU systems were recently installed by the Original Construction Contractor and are currently under an active, comprehensive installer and manufacturer warranty. Performing physical or software re-configuration through any third-party mechanical contractor would immediately void the remaining warranty, exposing the Government to significant financial liability for future system repairs or failures. Specialized Technical Familiarity: Having designed and built the mechanical integration of this facility, the Original Construction Contractor has unmatched technical familiarity with the custom piping geometry, flow dynamics, and specific electrical hookups of this site. Introducing a new vendor would require extensive duplicate diagnostics and system engineering, resulting in substantial duplicative costs and unacceptable delays. Response Instructions THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. However, in accordance with RFO publicizing and simplified commercial guidelines, any responsible source that believes it can fully meet the Government�s requirements may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the agency. All submissions must include: Company name, CAGE code, UEI, and socioeconomic status. A detailed technical narrative and supporting evidence demonstrating the vendor's ability to perform the HVAC re-configuration without voiding active manufacturer warranties or requiring proprietary programming keys. Pricing quote Responses must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer no later than 11 September 2026 at 12:00 PM EST.

title: Ground Station as a Service
description: This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is issued solely for market research purposes to identify capable small and large business entities and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotation (RFQ). This notice does not represent a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor shall the Government incur any financial obligation for information submitted in response hereto. No claim against the Government may arise from a response to this SSN or from the Government's use of any submitted information. Failure to respond to this SSN does not prohibit participation in any potential subsequent solicitation. The information contained herein is subject to revision and imposes no binding obligation upon the Government. All submitted materials shall become the property of the Government and will not be returned. Any proprietary or copyrighted information included in a response must be explicitly marked as such. Requirement: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information System (NESDIS), Office of Satellite and Mission Operations (OSPO) requires an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Ground Station as a Service (GSaaS) including site certification, telemetry downlink data services, and satellite commanding data services. This will satisfy NESDIS current requirements for commercial remote telemetry-only downlink for partner missions, Constellation Observing System for Meteorology Ionosphere and Climate-2 (COSMIC-2), Korea Multi-Purpose Satellite�5 (KOMPSAT-5), and PAZ. The GSaaS contract will provide agility for NESDIS to add or reduce ground station service task orders for future NESDIS or partner missions as they are defined. Under this contract, the contractor is responsible for operating ground status sites that meet strict geographical, technical, and regulatory requirements, including securing necessary radio frequency licenses. The contractor shall provide ancillary engineering support services, such as systems compatibility assessments and proficiency testing, while strictly complying with physical security programs, cybersecurity frameworks like NIST or ISO, and government data rights that restrict the external distribution of sensitive information without explicit permission. NAICS Code/Size Standard: The applicable NAICS code is 517810, All other Telecommunications with business size standard of $40M[RS1] . Key Criteria: Site Requirement - The Contractor shall deliver GSaaS capabilities across qualified operational sites, ensuring continuous compliance with satellite-to-ground communication specifications, required security baselines, mission geographic footprint targets, and have availability to meet the Government�s anticipated tasking schedule. Scheduling Requirement � The Contractor shall fulfill Government services requests in accordance with the scheduling interface agreements specified in each task order. The Contractor shall achieve a minimum 95% operational success rate for scheduled contacts. A contact is deemed successful only if it is attempted, successfully completed with an Eb/N0 margin greater than 3 dB, and results in data delivery to the designated NOAA Internet Point of Presence within 60 seconds of contact completion. Security Requirement � The Contractor shall provide artifacts that demonstrate that sites and services meet security requirements according to the security frameworks established by the Contractor and approved by the Government. Regulatory Requirement � The Contractor shall be solely responsible for local and international regulatory compliance related to occupancy and operation of the service sites and for providing the services from those sites. The contractor shall secure, maintain, and comply with radio frequency licenses for the services provided. [TTT2] Required Response Information: Capable small and large business vendors are requested to provide the following information in response to this SSN announcement: Company Name/Division, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, and website URL (if available). A single Point-of-Contact name, title, telephone number, and e-mail address. Unique Entity ID (UEI). Please note that companies must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be considered potential sources (SAM.gov). Business Size in relation to NAICS 517810 and any SBA socio-economic certifications. Demonstrated capabilities in meeting the needs of the Key Criteria listed above. Conflict of Interest: Please detail the extent to which the respondent is aware of any potential organizational conflict of interest issues related to this requirement. Response Format: In order to better assist in the review of responses to this SSN, respondents are encouraged to prepare a capabilities statement that does not exceed 10 pages. Response Submission Requirements and Deadline: Responses to this SSN should be submitted via e-mail attachments, received no later than 05:00 PM, EST, 11 September 2026 to: Contracting Officer: Trang Tran at Trang.tran@noaa.gov; and Contracting Specialist: Markita Simmonds at markita.simmonds@noaa.gov.

title: Pacific Environmental Science Centre (PESC) Roof Replacement Project, North Vancouver, British Columbia
description: Located on Burrard Inlet in North Vancouver, Pacific Environmental Science Centre (PESC) is a centre for the study of marine, estuarine and freshwater toxicology and chemistry, with specialization in salmonid toxicogenomic, bacterial source tracking, and marine water quality monitoring. The Centre works in partnership with B.C. Environment, Health Canada, Transport Canada, Fisheries and Oceans Canada and the University of Victoria. The Centre houses chemical analysis (inorganic & organic), toxicological and microbiological laboratories, plus mobile labs and equipment used in Environment and Climate Change Canada's (ECCC) monitoring, regulatory and environmental science programs. The role of the Centre is to provide a core capability in laboratory science services to ECCC’s Pacific & Yukon Region, to conduct field surveys, inspections and investigations, and to respond to environmental emergencies. The existing roofing systems throughout the facility have reached or exceeded their service life and exhibit deficiencies including membrane deterioration, failed flashings, ponding water, damaged drains, and deteriorated parapet conditions. Previous condition assessments and investigations identified the need for phased roof replacement and rehabilitation work to maintain building integrity and reduce the risk of water infiltration and operational disruption. This project involves replacement and rehabilitation of multiple low-slope roofing areas at PESC. The work includes removal and replacement of existing roofing systems, flashings, insulation, drains, sheet metal components, localized deck repairs, PolyMethyl MethAcrylate (PMMA) membrane applications, and associated ancillary work in accordance with the contract specifications and drawings: PESC Roof Replacement Specifications and Drawings. The objective of this project is for the Contractor to perform complete removal and replacement of designated roofing systems at the PESC facility in accordance with the Specifications, Drawings, and Contract Documents. The Contractor shall provide all labour, materials, equipment, supervision, and services necessary to deliver a fully compliant, watertight, code compliant roofing system with the specified warranties and quality assurance requirements. The Contractor must perform and complete the Work within the period commencing upon notification of acceptance of the offer and ending no later than March 31, 2027. There will be a site visit on Wednesday, August 26, at 11:00 A.M. PDT. Interested bidders are to meet at Pacific Environmental Science Centre (PESC) 2645 Dollarton Hwy, North Vancouver, British Columbia, V7H 1B1 at the front entrance. Bidders must be escorted by the Facility Maintenance Senior Technician while on site. Bidders must communicate with the ECCC Contracting Authority no later than August 25, 2026, at 1:00 p.m. PDT, by email at Helena.Lee@ec.gc.ca, to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders who do not confirm attendance and who do not provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend as required will not be allowed access to the site. The requirement is subject to the provisions of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). For additional information, interested suppliers should contact Helena Lee at; Helena.Lee@ec.gc.ca.

title: France – Construction work for buildings relating to health – Marché global sectoriel relatif au projet de construction neuve du centre hospitalier SMR (soins médicaux de réadaptation) de Maubreuil à Saint Herblain
description: Le Centre Hospitalier de Maubreuil offre une prise en charge en soins médicaux de réadaptation (SMR). Il dispose pour cela d’un plateau technique spécialisé de rééducation. Ce dernier prévoit d’augmenter sa capacité d’accueil, tant pour l’hospitalisation conventionnelle que pour l’hôpital de jour, tout en intégrant des spécialités en oncologie. Ce projet se matérialise par la construction d’un nouveau centre hospitalier sur un terrain nu, situé à proximité de l’Hôpital G&R Laennec à Saint-Herblain. Cette construction neuve devra accueillir 96 lits et 53 places, sur une surface utile programmée de 6 913 m². La présente consultation a pour objet la contractualisation d’un marché global sectoriel au sens de l’article L.2171-5 du Code de la Commande publique. Le marché regroupe d’une part l’ensemble des études de conception nécessaires à la réalisation des ouvrages, d’autre part, l’exécution de l’ensemble des travaux nécessaires à la réalisation de ces ouvrages, et enfin la maintenance et le gros entretien et renouvellement des ouvrages sur une période de 2 années, intégrant la durée de la garantie.

title: 66--Notice of Intent to Sole Source for AutoLab 2000
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source for AutoLab 2000 Notice of Intent to Sole Source for New England Research, Inc., for the purchase of an AutoLab 2000 servo-hydraulic, large bore triaxial system capable to perform versatile petrophysical and rock mechanics experimentation on both natural rocks and man-made materials at reservoir conditions (overburden pressure, pore pressure, and temperature). In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services, the Department of Energy (DOE), National Energy Technology Laboratory (NETL) intends to negotiate and award a purchase order on a sole source basis to New England Research, Inc., for an AutoLab 2000 servo-hydraulic, large bore triaxial system capable to perform versatile petrophysical and rock mechanics experimentation on both natural rocks and man-made materials at reservoir conditions (overburden pressure, pore pressure, and temperature). This is considered a sole source to New England Research, Inc. because, to the best of NETL�s knowledge, based on market research conducted, New England Research, Inc., is the only known source that can provide this product to the required specifications. The NER AutoLab 2000, with its unique multi-physics coupling capabilities, proprietary base plug and feedthrough integration, pore fluid compatibility, and data continuity and research standardization, is the only known commercial system that offers the complete integration of high-load/high-pressure triaxial mechanics with multi-physics in-situ diagnostics in a single, unified platform. No known potential alternate sources exist which could satisfy NETL�s requirement. This notice of intent is not a request or quote/proposal. Any interested party that believes it is capable of meeting the NETL requirement described herein may identify themselves and must provide evidence of their capability to fulfill the requirement being requested by 1300 PM ED on 09/11/2026. Responses must be submitted in writing to the Contract Specialist Stefanie Page, via email at stefanie.page@netl.doe.gov no later than the time and date noted above. Telephone responses and requests will not be received. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive procurement.

title: PLA Survey - Iowa River Basin, Cedar River, Cedar Rapids, IA, Cedar Rapids Flood Risk Management Project, Reach 2 Phase 2 Downtown
description: THIS IS A PROJECT LABOR AGREEMENT (PLA) SURVEY ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, REQUEST FOR QUOTE, OR INVITATION FOR BID. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Rock Island District has a requirement for a construction contract for the project known as: Iowa River Basin, Cedar River, Cedar Rapids, IA, Cedar Rapids Flood Risk Management Project, Reach 2 Phase 2 Downtown Floodwalls Project Description: The work includes, but is not limited to, construction of concrete floodwall, concrete stoplog floodwall and swing closure gate structures, and related concrete cast-in-place columns, footings, sheet pile cutoff wall, H-Piles; Type B, Type C, and Type D Micropiles; and concrete sill. Work also includes related pavement and utilities removal, and installation of storm sewer, catch basins, and manholes, trench drain inlets, concrete sidewalks, concrete trail, curb and gutter, and concrete pavement work, pavement striping, provision of stoplogs for floodwall and storage racking, trail lighting, segmental block retaining wall, and enclosure structures.
